nodes.original_theorem:
Attributed ASTIS-authored actual Gaussian Gibbs marginal centered compact-gradient-domain Poincare; faithful source coefficient and standing hypotheses retained.
Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C2, 0<α≤β, α‖a‖²≤D²V(x)[a,a]≤β‖a‖² for every x,a, η>0 and βη≤1. Define μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ,Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Then ν is a probability. There exists one densely defined closable real linear gradient G:L²(ν)⇀L²(ν;E), whose graph consists exactly of AE classes (φ,∇φ) for smooth compactly supported φ, and whose closure has closed graph. For every z in domḠ with ∫z dν=0, [α/(1+αη)]‖z‖²≤‖Ḡz‖². The same G is chosen before every such z. No caller normalization, curvature, Poincare, law, domain, convergence or extra moment certificate is assumed. This is the genuine compact-gradient closure formulation of the source marginal PI; equivalence with a separately defined weighted H1 remains open.

Actual objects: mu=tilt-volume(-V), J=law(X,X+sqrtetaZ), nu=J.snd; G exact smooth compact scalar/vector-L2 graph, actual closure and actual normalized mean.

nodes.reconstructed_theorem:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure and canonical volume measure. The zero-dimensional case is included. Let V : E -> R be twice continuously differentiable. Let alpha and beta be nonnegative real numbers with alpha > 0 and alpha <= beta, and let eta be real with eta > 0 and beta eta <= 1. Assume, for every x,v in E, that
alpha ||v||^2 <= (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] <= beta ||v||^2.
Here D(DV)(x)[v] is the derivative of the derivative of V at x applied to v, and its value is then applied to v again.
Define mu = volume.tilted(x -> -V(x)), using normalized exponential tilting. Thus the measure is the normalized exponential tilt of canonical volume by exp(-V); this is the actual named measure construction, with its normalization built into tilted. Define J to be the pushforward of mu tensor stdGaussian(E) under (x,w) -> (x, x + sqrt(eta) w), and define nu to be the second marginal of J. The standard Gaussian is on E and is independent of the mu coordinate in this product construction.
Then nu is a probability measure, and there exists one partially defined real linear operator G from L^2(nu; R) to L^2(nu; E) with all the following properties. Its domain is dense in L^2(nu; R). It is closable, and its graph-closure operator Gbar is closed. For every u in L^2(nu; R) and v in L^2(nu; E), (u,v) is in the graph of G if and only if there exists a single infinitely continuously differentiable compactly supported function phi : E -> R such that u = phi nu-almost everywhere and v = grad(phi) nu-almost everywhere, using the genuine Euclidean gradient of that same phi.
For this same G, for every z in the domain of Gbar, if integral z dnu = 0, then
[alpha / (1 + alpha eta)] ||z||_{L^2(nu; R)}^2 <= ||Gbar z||_{L^2(nu; E)}^2.
Elements of these L^2 spaces are almost-everywhere classes of strongly measurable square-integrable functions; the displayed integral uses the canonical representative of the scalar class. Gbar z is the actual closed derivative determined by the closure of the exact graph just specified. The density, closability, closedness and exact graph properties belong to the single existentially chosen operator before the universal quantification over centered z. No measure, kernel, domain, gradient operator, curvature certificate, Poincare certificate, moment certificate, or convergence certificate is provided as an additional hypothesis. The statement does not assert an independently defined weak-H^1 identification, surjectivity, inverse or square-root operators, dynamics, algorithmic mixing, a broader result, or a cost estimate.
